text: Through it, the marketplace gets a short summary of the customer: the level, the verified phone number, and a display name.

text: The address sits in the protected part of the record, with the passport data.

text: The bank's keys encrypt it, and every read of it is audited.

text: So there is exactly one way for an address to leave: a sharing request that Aziz approves.

text: Here is how it runs.
prefix: Here is how it runs.

text: The marketplace backend asks the platform for a sharing request, with its own marketplace token.

text: The platform first checks two things.
prefix: The platform first checks two things.

text: Is Aziz at level two?

text: And is his marketplace account linked?

text: If either answer is no, the platform does not ask him.

text: It tells the marketplace to send Aziz to the mobile bank first.

text: Aziz is at level two, and his account is linked, so the request goes on.

text: The platform keeps it for the configured waiting time, and sends a push signal to the mobile bank.
prefix: The platform keeps it for the configured waiting time, and sends a push signal to the mobile bank.

text: Again, the push carries only the request identifier.
prefix: Again, the push carries only the request identifier.

text: The mobile bank pulls the request, and asks one question.
prefix: The mobile bank pulls the request, and asks one question.

text: Share your verified address with the marketplace?

text: Aziz taps Share.
prefix: Aziz taps Share.

text: Now the platform reads the address from the protected record, for one purpose: address sharing.

text: It writes an audit event that names the reader, the marketplace, and the purpose.

text: The marketplace collects the address one time, and saves it.

text: The bookshelf has a place to go.

text: Now the other answers.

text: If Aziz taps Refuse, nothing is saved, and the marketplace gets a refusal.
